placements.why: The ruling articulates an explicit architectural design trade-off: choosing server-side single-bundle delivery per run per person and rejecting client-side collapsing to avoid transferring the ordering burden to the reader.
placements.title: Architectural trade-offs, selected patterns, and rejected alternatives
placements.frame: What architectural alternatives were evaluated, and why was the chosen approach preferred over the rejected alternatives?

placements.why: Establishes the normative architectural theme that multi-skill reactions must route through a single bundle per run per recipient, enforcing a strict batching window tied to run close and rejecting per-skill delivery to protect reader focus.
placements.title: Reaction delivery bundles strictly per run per person to shield recipients from fragmentation
placements.frame: How should reaction notifications be aggregated across multi-skill execution runs to minimize cognitive burden on the recipient?
